anchors.claim: psi:X->R strictly convex, differentiable on nonempty int X. B_psi:X x int X->R; B(a;b)=psi(a)-psi(b)-<grad psi(b),a-b>. No value outside this carrier is defined here.

anchors.region: Opening distance-generating-function paragraph and nonnegativity/strict-support paragraph
anchors.claim: B is nonnegative for both arguments in int X by convexity; stronger paragraph explicitly asserts psi(a)>=psi(b)+<grad psi(b),a-b> for all a in X and fixed b in int X, equality only a=b. Therefore B>=0 on the full defined carrier. Reference point dependence and lack of symmetry are stated.

anchors.region: Immediate-lemma introductory paragraph, Lemma 6.7, citation and display
anchors.claim: For x,y in int X and z in X: B(z;x)+B(x;y)-B(z;y)=<grad psi(y)-grad psi(x),z-x>. Attributed to Chen and Teboulle (1993). No written proof follows on this page or before section 6.4 on the next page.
V nonempty convex, x* in V, f convex and differentiable on an open set containing V. x* minimizes f on V iff <grad f(x*),y-x*>>=0 for all y in V.
Gradient-square terms arise from output before observing loss; they become nonpositive if observing loss before output. Explicit cross-reference Section15.5.1.

Nonempty closed convex V subset X subset R^d; strictly convex psi differentiable on int X; x0 in int X, not stated in V; eta1,...,etaT>0. Receive extended-real loss with V subset dom loss, select xt in argmin_V loss_t+eta_t^-1 B(.;x_(t-1)), then pay loss at xt.

anchors.region: Theorem15.30 statement hypotheses from Let psi through for t=1,...,T, before Then
anchors.claim: psi differentiable on int X, closed, strictly convex; nonempty closed convex V subset X; xt in int X, losses subdifferentiable on V; eta_(t+1)<=eta_t for t=1,...,T as printed. Positive eta and x0 in int X inherited from Algorithm15.8. Thus the source supplies all reference-point interiority needed in this theorem. For u in V, u is in X. No source-domain gap is asserted.

anchors.region: Theorem15.30 first conclusion beginning Then and its first display
anchors.claim: Under src:T15.30-premises and Algorithm15.8, for all u in V, regret <= max_(0<=t<=T-1) B(u;xt)/eta_T - sum_(t=1)^T B(xt;x_(t-1))/eta_t.
For eta_t=eta, t=1,...,T, regret <= B(u;x0)/eta - sum_(t=1)^T B(xt;x_(t-1))/eta. This is a second theorem conclusion, not a consequence of maximizing a variable-step bound.

source_semantics.space: finite-dimensional R^d with Euclidean gradient pairing; source loss may take +infinity away from V
source_semantics.initialization: x0 in int X only, no x0 in V requirement in Algorithm15.8
source_semantics.later_iterates: x_t in V by actual argmin selection and in int X by separate T15.30 assumption
source_semantics.comparator: every u in V, hence finite loss there and first B argument in X
source_semantics.feedback: observe full loss function before predicting and paying it
source_semantics.probability: deterministic pathwise guarantee; no probability, filtration or expectation stated
source_semantics.normalization: eta times one-step loss difference; three divergence terms with coefficient +1,-1,-1
source_semantics.fixed_terminal: author statement drops terminal; author supplies no fixed-step proof
source_semantics.variable_terminal: author exact summation has -B(u;xT)/etaT, subsequently dropped using nonnegativity

proposed_derived_interface.claim: Let E be a real normed vector space, V convex, f,psi:E->R, f convex on V, p,u in V, eta>0. Let x in E, not necessarily V, and assume psi Frechet differentiable at x and p. Supply p as an actual global minimizer over V of f(y)+eta^-1 B(y;x), where B(a;b)=psi(a)-psi(b)-Dpsi(b)(a-b). Then eta(f(p)-f(u))<=B(u;x)-B(u;p)-B(p;x). No f differentiability is required.
